content: 1. Ivacaftor metabolism is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. If co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the ivacaftor dose should be reduced. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 2. Vonoprazan reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Administer vonoprazan at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after ketoconazole. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 5. Clarithromycin increases lacosamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and lapatinib prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 8. Lenacapavir increases clarithromycin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 9. Clarithromycin and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 10. Clarithromycin increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 11. Leuprolide increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 12. Clarithromycin and levalbuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially requiring dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 14. Clarithromycin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Clarithromycin increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Due to lumacaftor's induction effect on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to 1 tablet daily for the first week to allow for lumacaftor's steady-state induction effect. After this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the dose to 5 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Decrease maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of marijuana by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Both mavorixafor and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. 27. Clarithromycin and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of midazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor; caution is advised with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This combination may also prolong the QT interval. Use alternatives if available. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 32. Mitotane decreases clarithromycin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 33. Clarithromycin increases momelotinib toxicity due to OATP1B1/B3 inhibition. Use caution and monitor therapy.
